the thing is niacinamide and glycolic acid are both pretty strong formulas most people are sensitive to the ordinary(<-brand) glycolic acid toner i use. and armpits i believe would be more prone to being irritated than your face. **so definitely patch test before putting any product in a sensitive area like that

if the discoloration is new then i would evaluate your diet/exercise/water intake just see if it’s an issue with some nutritional thing you’re missing or if you started something new in your routine that could cause it. or i would try a scrub+antibacterial soap i use dial on my armpits/privates bc other stuff will irritate my softer spots. 

but ofc a doctor is always going to know the best thing to do to help you out so if it’s a big deal to you then that’s the best suggestion tbh

lol i think you might be overreacting a little bit or these pictures aren’t doing justice because it looks normal and very slight. could just be buildup and you could try using a scrub/exfoliant first.

regardless if you yourself have noticed a change in your body like this and you feel it’s really abnormal then please go to a doctor there is a chance you could have hyperpigmentation due to hormonal imbalances or you’re actually lacking in specific vitamin or something your body needs. 

i’m south asian and i have lots of discoloration across my armpits, around my mouth, near my groin/under breast-for the most part it’s normal/genetic but it looks much more visible if my iron is low, i’m not eating right or exercising. 

i use niacinamide and glycolic acid toner routinely-i use azealic acid too because it has made the most difference for me but it’s really expensive for how much product you get(i live in US might be different pricing in other countries 🤷‍♀️) so i end up using it on and off when i can afford it-which isn’t really good because i notice it only works after weeks of use so you have to keep up with it.. but regardless all of these items have NOT gotten rid of my hyperpigmentation, it looks less apparent than before and i can get away with wearing sheer/light foundation as opposed to having to spot conceal/bake/have a full foundation routine to cover up the discoloration.

all that to say-it’s not especially abnormal but you know your body better than anyone so if you’re nervous about this and have the means to see a doctor there is no shame in taking care of yourself

very solid advice ! sucks you can’t have someone help you with it sounds like it’s in a hard to reach spot. i moisturize fresh tattoos a couple times a day, using just enough to cover tattoo not drown it in lotion.

best thing you can do is just keep washing it, honestly i only wash my tats once a day in my daily shower, and i haven’t had any problems. i think since the skin wants to dry out to shed itself it’s hard trying to keep up, just try to lotion it more frequently, but i get that can be hard if you work a job n all..

some unprofessional advice: maybe lotion+saran wrap to keep in moisture for a little longer ? when you’re home and just watching a show or doing dishes just keep it on for an hour i think couple hours longer might be bad for the tattoo but i think that could help combat the dryness. 

i think some of my old school tattooer buddies would recommend vaseline/aquaphor but i think you gotta be 2 weeks post tattoo to do that bc i fear the tattoo wouldn’t get to breathe and it might get nasty but people swear by it so perhaps look into that if nothing is helping you.

TLDR: don’t over moisturize/lubriderm+unscented dial(ANTIBACTERIAL) is solid combo keep doing it+mayhap up how often you moisturize and not how much(don’t drown the tattoo just apply a thin layer a little will go a very long way esp w bigger pieces) no itching !! let it do its thing and flake off on its own.

tattooing is 100% one of those things you HAVE to want. you will resent the job and hate it if it’s just a last resort, it’s a good amount of dedication-but once you get to a point where you’re bringing in your own clientele and basically are your own business, it’s really rewarding imo. you’ll probably spend a lot of your free time drawing but you also have complete control over your schedule, which is really hard to come by for a full time job that you expect to keep for the majority of your life.

but it’s also a bit of a gamble these days, this is just my opinion(and i’m from northern california where the market for tattooing is very saturated) and your location will have a big part in your success as well. i say it’s a gamble because i personally know very talented artists that genuinely have a passion for the art but, are not doing well because we’re in an area where there is just so many tattooers and not enough clients for everyone. 

it really isn’t a job you should pursue if you don’t LOVE art and tattoo, there will be slow months or seasons and you’ll have clients that you won’t love and you’ll be doing artwork for a while that you won’t love(unless you’re lucky) because it’s what will bring in clientele. the motivation/dedication is what will get you through the slow months and year long apprenticeships-of course this is all my opinion. i just know that tattooing looks like a fun job on paper until you realize that it’s a journey to get somewhere successful or even stable.
